title: Liability slider + indemnity presets: decision playbook and pricing experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Sales and Legal are repeatedly re-opening MSA/DPA negotiations over indemnity and liability caps, causing multi-week delays and unpredictable price concessions. We need a documented playbook + decision surface that lets Sales self-serve low-risk concessions and ties liability changes to an automated pricing adjustment experiment so revenue and legal risk are both visible and measurable.
acceptance_criteria: A public internal playbook exists describing: standard indemnity language, three liability cap tiers, and approval thresholds for each tier
Sales UI copy and guidance (for SDRs/AEs) drafted and validated by Legal and Sales Ops
Backend flagging to record chosen liability tier and indemnity template in the contract metadata for telemetry
Pricing experiment configured that adjusts recommended discount based on selected liability tier; experiment hypothesis and metric definitions documented
Two pilot deals completed by EPD and Sales with playbook applied and post-mortem notes recorded
tasks: Workshop with Legal to finalize indemnity presets and three liability tiers (None / Standard / Extended)
Draft Sales-facing decision tree and quick reference (1-pager)
Implement contract metadata fields in Contract UI (liability_tier, indemnity_preset)
Hook telemetry: event contract_redline.accepted with tier and discount applied
Define and deploy pricing experiment in Growth/Trials with control and two treatment arms
Pilot with two Enterprise reps and capture time-to-close and concession size
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stricter default caps reduce legal risk but may push larger customers to ask for exceptions — mitigation = transparent price signal
Legal prefers template-based approach to free-text negotiation — avoids clause drift across contracts
We will not attempt to automate final legal sign-off; goal is to reduce low-risk queue volume and make exceptions traceable
If experiment shows >20% revenue leakage for higher tiers after 2 months, pause and re-evaluate price offsets
